title: Sanders Urges Democrats to Focus on Economic Relief Over Endless Trump Investigations
snippet: Following midterm victories, Sen. Bernie Sanders cautioned Democrats against spending all their energy probing President Donald Trump, calling instead for a bold focus on working-class economic issues.
content:
WASHINGTON — Fresh off midterm victories, Sen. Bernie Sanders is issuing a clear warning to his fellow Democrats: Don't let your mandate get swallowed up by endless investigations into President Donald Trump.

Speaking Sunday on NBC’s Meet the Press, the Vermont progressive acknowledged that oversight is crucial, but stressed that addressing the skyrocketing cost of living for American families must take priority.

“We cannot spend all of our time investigating Trump,” Sanders said. “We've got to stand up for working-class families, make a real difference in their lives.”

Prioritizing the Kitchen Table

Democrats campaigned heavily on economic pressures ahead of the midterms, hammering the Trump administration over high prices for groceries, gas, housing, and medical care. However, some party members are preparing to pivot aggressively toward oversight. Incoming House Oversight Committee leader Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) signaled plans to launch broad inquiries into executive pardons and key administration figures, including Elon Musk and Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.

Sanders urged restraint, insisting that voters are demanding bold policy action rather than political warfare.

“What I think this election was about, is the American people not only expressing disgust with Trump and his policies, but are demanding real change, no more tinkering around the edges,” Sanders said, pointing out that voters are working longer hours while struggling to afford basic necessities.

Targeted Oversight and Potential Cooperation

While Sanders advocated against overreaching probes, he made an exception for high-stakes Cabinet accountability. Appearing on CNN’s State of the Union, the member of the Senate HELP Committee declared Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. to be “the most dangerous secretary of the HHS in history.” Sanders expressed openness to impeachment efforts championed by incoming lawmakers, promising tough committee hearings ahead.

Yet, Sanders also held out hope for potential legislative progress, characterizing Trump as an “erratic” but opportunistic leader who might be persuaded to back populist measures.

“I think, when Trump looks out in the world and he sees millions of people working for starvation wages, he might not be unsympathetic to raising the minimum wage to a living wage,” Sanders suggested, adding that the president might also be enticed by the credit of expanding national healthcare access.
